# N01 — Non-gating active-marker: display-only reads across the artifact boundary

**Type:** `adr`. Observability reads precisely the inside-phase detail the artifact boundary
withholds from Layer 1, so the reconciliation is a real architectural decision and is settled before
the cross-repo marker contract is picked up.

> **▶ On pickup — before N03:** record the decision through the ADR discipline. Run the plan-review
> gate: this is a one-way-door rule on shared infrastructure (the supervisor↔pack boundary, ADR
> 0002 / 0030) that every future "show inside-phase detail" feature will cite.
> **Blocks:** N03 — the marker contract must obey the display-only invariant and have its carrier
> (OQ-3) settled before any skill writes the pointer.

## What

Record, as a new ADR, the invariant that lets the swimlanes view exist without breaking the
artifact boundary: the `_active` step/persona marker is read by Layer 1 **for display only** — no
advancement, halt, grade, retry, exit-code, or stop-guard decision may read it. It is to the
swimlane what a run-log timestamp is to the run record: Layer-2-authored content the supervisor may
*show* but never *decide on*. The ADR also settles the marker's **carrier** (design-doc OQ-3 — a
supervisor-written `active.json` field versus a pack-authored `exec-state.json` `_active` pointer)
against ADR 0030's pack-ownership rule, and the **last-writer rule** for parallel persona writes
from Claude-Code sub-agents (OQ-2).

## Why

The assumption being tested: a single sanctioned "display-only reads across the boundary" pattern
keeps the supervisor content-blind for every *decision* while letting it read the marker only to
display it on screen — so the feature stays inside architecture §5 and stays worker-agnostic (ADR
0011). The rejected alternative
is letting the renderer read whatever it needs ad hoc, which silently grows supervisor knowledge of
phases and erodes "done means done" enforced from artifacts alone. Accepting this unlocks N03;
until it lands, the marker schema would encode an unsettled carrier and an undecided gating rule.

## Completion

**Decision:** the active-marker is a non-gating, display-only signal; Layer 1 may render it but no
decision path may import its reader. Recorded as a new ADR (next free number, 0031) with context and
consequences, citing ADR 0002 / 0030 and architecture §5, and naming the enforcement: NFR-3's
fault-injection test plus a guard test asserting no decision path imports the marker reader. The ADR
settles OQ-3 (carrier + N01-grader schema-compat) and OQ-2 (last-writer rule), and states that the
pattern is reusable for future inside-phase-display features. ADRs carry no Linear ticket
references. The `delivery-shape` skill does not restate the ADR template — that discipline lives in
the ADR skill.

## Assumptions

- `exec-state.json` reads already ignore unknown keys, so an additive `_active` pointer is backward-compatible with `handoff.read*` and the N01 grader. *(to-verify)*
- A free ADR number is available at 0031 (0001–0030 exist). *(verified)*
- The display-only invariant is enforceable by a static guard test (no decision module imports the marker reader). *(to-verify)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** the carrier choice (active.json vs exec-state.json) is made wrong and forces a second
  schema edit once skills write it. *Falsifier:* if a pack-authored `exec-state.json` pointer cannot
  pass the N01-grader schema-compat review, the active.json field is the carrier — record the reader
  ownership in the ADR before N03.
- **Risk:** "non-gating" is asserted but not enforced, and a later change quietly reads the marker
  in a decision path. *Mitigation:* the ADR mandates the guard test; N02/N03 land it, and review
  treats any decision-path import of the marker reader as a boundary violation.

## Tasks

- [ ] Frame the non-gating invariant for the ADR: display-only reads across the artifact boundary; the marker is Layer-2-authored content the supervisor shows but never decides on. Done when: the problem, the invariant, and the boundary citation (ADR 0002 / 0030, architecture §5) are written into the ADR draft. Model: Frontier · risk one-way · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·H·L·H·L · companions code-review-and-quality
- [ ] Settle the marker carrier (OQ-3): supervisor-written `active.json` field vs pack-authored `exec-state.json` `_active` pointer, resolved against ADR 0030, with the N01-grader schema-compat review. Done when: the ADR names the carrier and the field's reader/writer owner, and the schema-compat verdict is recorded. Model: Frontier · risk one-way · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·H·L
- [ ] Settle the last-writer / merge rule (OQ-2) for parallel persona writes from Claude-Code sub-agents. Done when: the ADR states whether `_active.persona` is one value or a set and which write wins. Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·L·M·L
- [ ] Record the enforcement and run the plan-review gate to acceptance: NFR-3 fault-injection plus a guard test that no decision path imports the marker reader. Done when: the ADR names both tests as the invariant's fitness functions and a plan-review reference is filed with the decision accepted. # N03 — Marker contract: persona depth on every worker

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** the swimlane to show the active review persona on any
> worker — not just Claude Code — by reading a marker the pack writes, **so that** I can read
> `review / security-auditor` at the moment it is true regardless of which model runs the work.

> **▶ On pickup — before coding:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build agent's
> at-pickup task breakdown phase.
> **Blocked by:** N01 (the display-only invariant + the settled carrier and last-writer rule) and
> N02 (the proven step-derivation path this falls back to when no marker is present).

This is the **cross-repo** slice. The `_active` step/persona pointer is written by the `exec:*`
skills in `agent-skills-shaper` (co-located with the existing `exec-state.json` section writes — see
Assumptions); the renderer prefers the marker and falls back to N02's stream path where none is
present. This is what delivers persona depth on **every** worker (NFR-6) and makes the view
rename-proof and stream-internal-independent.

## What

Add the `_active` step/persona pointer to the `exec:*` skills under the carrier N01 settled, and
switch the renderer to prefer it over the slice-1 stream path. Capture the residual OQ-1 evidence (a
real `exec:review` persona dispatch, Path B) and prove persona depth on both a Claude-Code worker
and a codex worker. Handle the marker-miss and stale-marker paths so an old pack or a forgetful
skill degrades cleanly rather than blocking.

## Why

The assumption being tested: putting persona identity on a pack-authored marker — not the stream —
is the only way to get persona depth on non-Claude workers (inline personas emit no tool boundary)
and to decouple the view from Claude-Code's tool taxonomy. The rejected alternative is extending the slice-1 stream
parse to personas (design-doc Alt 2 alone): it dies on non-Claude workers and couples the UI to
stream internals, failing NFR-6. This closes KR1 — the worker-agnostic persona-during-review case
the whole feature is measured on.

## Completion

- **Done when:** during a live drain the swimlane shows the correct active persona during `review`
  read from the `_active` marker, on **both** a Claude-Code worker and a codex worker (NFR-6).
- **Done when:** when no marker is present (old pack), the renderer falls back to the N02 stream path
  for step depth and degrades persona to Claude-only, verified with an old-pack fixture (rollback
  step 3).
- **Done when:** the pack's marker write is one sub-1 KB file write per step/persona transition with
  no added network calls (NFR-5), asserted by the pack's contract test.
- **Done when:** a stale marker (skill forgot to clear) triggers the log-only staleness warning and
  a dimmed last-known active node, never blocking the run (NFR-3).

# N04 — Full stepper chain: done / active / upcoming

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** the stepper to show the whole `exec:*` chain at once —
> done, active, and upcoming — **so that** I can see where the run is in the *whole* journey, not just
> the steps it has already walked.

> **▶ On pickup — before coding:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build agent's
> at-pickup task breakdown phase.

This rides the proven slice-1 strip — still one line, no owned region, no cross-repo work. Today the
strip shows only *visited* steps plus the active one (prior steps collapse to `·`, upcoming steps are
invisible); this node renders the full canonical chain so the operator sees what is done versus
upcoming, the design doc's stated behaviour that N02 deferred.

## What

Render against a canonical ordered chain instead of `tracker.history`. Define the chain once —
`pickup → breakdown → build → review → verify → simplify → finish`, with `debug` shown inline only
when entered (an escalation, not a fixed slot) — and mark each step done `●` / active `◉` /
upcoming `○` from the active step (`_effective_active`) and the visited set. The two signal sources
disagree on names — the stream gives `exec:pickup`, the `_active` marker gives bare `review` — so a
single normalization helper strips the `exec:` prefix and maps both onto the same chain slot, by
construction rather than by two parallel rules.

## Why

The assumption being tested: the operator's trust comes from seeing the *whole* path, and the chain
is fixed and known, so the renderer can draw upcoming steps without any new signal — a pure local
change on the already-proven strip. The rejected alternative is leaving the chain stream-derived
(visited-only): it cannot show what has not happened yet, which is half of "done versus upcoming."
This is the cheapest, lowest-risk gap to close and ships value before the owned region (N07) is
built.

## Completion

- **Done when:** a synthetic step sequence renders every canonical step with the correct
  done/active/upcoming mark within one transition of ground truth (NFR-1), `debug` appearing inline
  only once entered.
- **Done when:** a stream `exec:pickup` and a bare-`pickup` `_active` marker resolve to the same
  chain slot through the one normalization helper.
- **Done when:** a non-TTY render of the full chain emits zero ANSI control sequences and zero stdout
  bytes (NFR-4), and the disable switch still reverts to today's flat stream.

## Assumptions

- The canonical chain is fixed and complete (`pickup → … → finish`, `debug`/`simplify` as
  escalations) and matches the pack's `exec:*` workflow. *(to-verify)*
- `_effective_active` and `tracker.history` together carry enough to classify every step as
  done/active/upcoming without a new signal. *(verified)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** the stream and marker name systems are reconciled wrong, so a step shows in the wrong slot
  or twice. *Mitigation:* one normalization helper is the single source of truth, covered by a test
  asserting both name forms map to one slot.
- **Risk:** a pack renames or reorders an `exec:*` step and the hard-coded chain drifts, blanking or
  misplacing a step. *Falsifier:* if the chain cannot be sourced from the pack's workflow, a renamed
  step renders as an unknown inline node rather than corrupting the fixed chain — verify with a
  renamed-step fixture.

# N06 — Richer keyboard controls: navigate and follow-toggle

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** to walk the queue with `↑/↓` and toggle auto-follow
> with `f`, **so that** I can hold my view on one issue's swimlane without losing my place when the
> running issue changes.

> **▶ On pickup — before coding:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build agent's
> at-pickup task breakdown phase.

The strip already maps digit keys `1`–`9` to focus and `0` to clear, on top of the focus machinery
(`focus_issue`, `_resolve_focus`). This node adds relative navigation and a follow toggle. Pause is
deliberately out of scope — a live `claude` cannot be paused; the ticket records why.

## What

Extend `KeyboardListener.handle_key` on the existing focus machinery: `↑/↓` (or `j/k`) move focus to
the previous or next queue item; `f` toggles auto-follow — on, the view follows the running issue
(today's default); off, it holds the manual selection; `q` signals the listener to stop, cosmetically,
never killing the run. Arrow keys arrive as escape sequences (`\x1b[A`), so the cbreak read loop
needs minimal multi-byte handling.

## Why

The assumption being tested: relative navigation and a follow toggle are the controls the operator
reaches for once the queue has more than a handful of issues, and they sit directly on the focus
machinery slice 1 already built — no new state. The rejected alternative is leaving only absolute
digit-focus: it does not scale past nine issues and offers no way to hold a view against auto-follow.
This stays on the current single-line queue, so it carries no owned-region dependency.

## Completion

- **Done when:** `handle_key` for `↑`/`↓` moves focus to the previous/next queue item and `f` toggles
  between follow-the-running-issue and hold-the-selection, driven through the `handle_key` test seam.
- **Done when:** `q` signals the listener to stop with `WorkerResult` and the exit code unchanged
  (NFR-3 — the control is cosmetic, never a kill).
- **Done when:** a non-TTY stdin constructs no thread and no termios state — byte-for-byte equivalent
  to never constructing the listener.

## Assumptions

- `focus_issue` / `_resolve_focus` already express both the auto-follow default and an explicit hold,
  so the toggle needs only a flag, not new focus state. *(verified)*
- Arrow-key escape sequences can be read in the existing cbreak loop with minimal multi-byte
  buffering. *(to-verify)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** multi-byte escape parsing misreads an arrow as separate `\x1b` / `[` / `A` keystrokes and
  mis-routes focus. *Mitigation:* the cbreak loop buffers the escape sequence; the `handle_key` seam
  is tested with the full sequence and with a bare `\x1b`.
- **Risk:** a new control path reaches into the run and stops it, breaking the non-gating ceiling.
  *Falsifier:* a `q` keystroke that changes the exit code means the listener is wired to execution —
  it must only set its own stop event.

## Tasks

- [ ] Extend `handle_key` with `↑/↓` (previous/next focus) and `f` (auto-follow toggle) on the existing focus machinery, buffering arrow escape sequences in the cbreak loop. Done when: `handle_key` for `↑`/`↓` moves focus to the adjacent queue item and `f` toggles follow vs hold, via the `handle_key` seam. Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·L·L·L
- [ ] Add `q` as a cosmetic listener stop and keep the non-TTY no-op. Done when: `q` signals the listener stop with the exit code unchanged (NFR-3) and a non-TTY stdin constructs no thread (byte-for-byte parity). Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = L·L·L·M·L

# N07 — Owned multi-line status region (DECSTBM)

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** the status view to hold a stable multi-line region that
> the scrolling worker log cannot corrupt, **so that** the queue, stepper, and persona fan-out can
> share the screen with the live log without smearing into each other.

> **▶ On pickup — before N08, N09, N11:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build
> agent's at-pickup task breakdown phase. This is the **foundational** node for D2's richer panes.
> **Blocks:** N08, N09, N11 — each renders into the region this node establishes.

This settles the design doc's render decision (OQ-4) a second time, for the richer view. Slice 1
answered OQ-4 with a one-to-two-line strip redrawn by cursor-up, which assumes the cursor sits where
the renderer left it — a worker log line landing mid-redraw corrupts a taller block. This node owns a
region the log cannot reach, and it carries the integration risk for every richer pane, so its first
task exercises the real seam against a live stream.

## What

Pin the bottom N lines as a fixed status region with a DEC scroll region (DECSTBM, `\x1b[<top>;<bottom>r`)
and paint the status block with absolute cursor positioning while the worker passthrough scrolls in
the region above. The decision recorded in-node: a DECSTBM scroll region, not `rich.Live` or an
alternate screen — it is the only mechanism that keeps the append-only passthrough visible (the
property slice 1 protects), cohabits with the log (they never share cursor space), and stays inside
the fitness contracts. Its new cost is real and in scope: the region must reset on every exit path
(clean teardown and crash/kill), and re-pin on terminal resize.

## Why

The assumption being tested: a fixed bottom region driven by DECSTBM lets a multi-line status block
coexist with the scrolling worker log without the regression `rich.Live` would force (owning the
cursor, suppressing the passthrough). The rejected alternative is the alternate-screen buffer with
the passthrough suppressed: it reaches full prototype fidelity but drops the live `│` diagnostics the
operator relies on — a visibility regression the design deliberately avoided. Proving the region here
retires the render risk before N08/N09/N11 pay to fill it.

## Completion

- **Done when:** during a live drain the status block holds in a fixed bottom region while the
  `AgentSink` passthrough scrolls above it without corrupting the block, on a real TTY.
- **Done when:** the scroll region is released (`\x1b[r`) on normal teardown, on Ctrl-C, and on a
  killed worker — asserted by a teardown test — leaving the terminal with no residual region.
- **Done when:** a `SIGWINCH` during a live render re-pins the region to the new terminal size with
  the status block intact.
- **Done when:** the non-TTY render emits zero bytes (NFR-4), the passthrough sink bytes are
  byte-identical to a feature-off run, and an injected render fault leaves the exit code unchanged
  (NFR-3) — all for the multi-line region.

## Assumptions

- A DECSTBM scroll region keeps the worker passthrough confined to the scrolling area without
  changing the bytes `AgentSink` writes. *(to-verify)*
- The kill path can reach a region-reset before the terminal is handed back (an `atexit` or signal
  handler fires on the process-group kill). *(to-verify)*
- `shutil.get_terminal_size()` plus a `SIGWINCH` handler is enough to re-pin on resize without a full
  terminal-capability library. *(to-verify)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** a crash or kill skips the region reset and leaves the operator's shell wedged in a pinned
  region. *Mitigation:* the reset is registered on both the clean teardown seam and an
  `atexit`/signal handler; the teardown test asserts a reset on the kill path. This is the node's main
  risk.
- **Risk:** the passthrough and the renderer race on the same stderr and the absolute-positioned write
  lands inside the scrolling region. *Falsifier:* if the block corrupts under concurrent passthrough,
  the region is not actually confining the log — re-confirm the DECSTBM top/bottom bounds before
  building N08.
- **Risk:** a terminal that ignores DECSTBM (or a non-VT pipe) renders the block wrong. *Mitigation:*
  every escape stays behind the TTY check (NFR-4), so a non-TTY degrades to the flat stream with zero
  control bytes.

## Tasks

- [ ] `skeleton` — pin a fixed bottom region with DECSTBM against a real drain stream and paint the existing queue+stepper into it while the passthrough scrolls above, toolchain (terminal-size read) folded in. Done when: a live TTY drain holds the status block in the bottom region while `AgentSink` passthrough scrolls above without corrupting it. Model: Frontier · risk reversible · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·M·H·L · companions code-review-and-quality
- [ ] Guarantee region reset on every exit: clean teardown plus an `atexit`/signal-handler reset for the crash and kill paths. Done when: the region is released on normal teardown, on Ctrl-C, and on a killed worker — asserted by a teardown test — with no residual region. Model: Frontier · risk reversible · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·M·H·L · companions code-review-and-quality
- [ ] Re-pin the region on terminal resize via `SIGWINCH` and a terminal-size read. Done when: a `SIGWINCH` during a live render re-pins the region to the new size with the status block intact. Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·M·M·L
- [ ] `acceptance` — keep the fitness contracts green for the owned region. Done when: the NFR-4 zero-bytes, byte-identical-passthrough parity, and NFR-3 fault-injection tests all pass for the multi-line region. Model: Frontier · risk reversible · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·L·H·L · companions code-review-and-quality

# N07 — Owned multi-line status region (DECSTBM)

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** the status view to hold a stable multi-line region that
> the scrolling worker log cannot corrupt, **so that** the queue, stepper, and persona fan-out can
> share the screen with the live log without smearing into each other.

This settles the design doc's render decision (OQ-4) a second time, for the richer view. Slice 1
answered OQ-4 with a one-to-two-line strip redrawn by cursor-up, which assumes the cursor sits where
the renderer left it — a worker log line landing mid-redraw corrupts a taller block. This node owns a
region the log cannot reach, and it carries the integration risk for every richer pane, so its first
task exercises the real seam against a live stream.

## What

Pin the bottom N lines as a fixed status region with a DEC scroll region (DECSTBM, `\x1b[<top>;<bottom>r`)
and paint the status block with absolute cursor positioning while the worker passthrough scrolls in
the region above. The decision recorded in-node: a DECSTBM scroll region, not `rich.Live` or an
alternate screen — it is the only mechanism that keeps the append-only passthrough visible (the
property slice 1 protects), cohabits with the log (they never share cursor space), and stays inside
the fitness contracts. Its new cost is real and in scope: the region must reset on every exit path
(clean teardown and crash/kill), and re-pin on terminal resize.

## Why

The assumption being tested: a fixed bottom region driven by DECSTBM lets a multi-line status block
coexist with the scrolling worker log without the regression `rich.Live` would force (owning the
cursor, suppressing the passthrough). The rejected alternative is the alternate-screen buffer with
the passthrough suppressed: it reaches full prototype fidelity but drops the live `│` diagnostics the
operator relies on — a visibility regression the design deliberately avoided. Proving the region here
retires the render risk before N08/N09/N11 pay to fill it.

  `AgentSink` passthrough scrolls above it without corrupting the block, on a real TTY.

- **Done when:** a `SIGWINCH` during a live render re-pins the region to the new terminal size with
  the status block intact.

# N08 — Richer queue rows: title, status, counter

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** each queue row to name its issue and its status — title,
> running step, PR link, or what it waits on — with a done/total counter, **so that** I can read the
> whole cycle's state at a glance instead of decoding a row of glyphs.

> **▶ On pickup — before coding:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build agent's
> at-pickup task breakdown phase.
> **Blocked by:** N07 — the multi-row queue renders into the owned region N07 establishes.

The queue is one line of glyphs and IDs today. This node makes it the prototype's multi-row pane:
glyph + ID + title + per-state status text and a `{done}/{n}` header. Most of the data is already in
hand at queue-build time; only the PR URL arrives later in the lifecycle.

## What

Grow `QueueItem` (today `identifier` + `state`) with `title` and `blocked_by`, populated at
queue-build from `plan.order`'s `title` and `blockers` — a pure local change, no new fetch. Thread
`pr_urls` into the item at the done-transition (`_mark_queue`) from the handoff data already read.
Render each row with its title and per-state status (`running · <active step>`, `queued · after
<deps>`, `done · <pr-url>`) and a `{done}/{n}` header, in pick order — never re-sorted — inside the
owned region. Add the new fields with defaults so existing construction sites and tests stay valid.

## Why

The assumption being tested: the queue's title, dependencies, and PR link are already available to
the orchestrator (`plan.order` and the handoff read), so the richer pane is plumbing existing data
into `QueueItem`, not a new data source. The rejected alternative is having the renderer re-derive
order or status from a different rule than the orchestrator picks — the queue would then lie about
execution order. Pick order stays the single source of truth.

## Completion

- **Done when:** a mixed-state queue renders each row with its title, the correct per-state status
  text, and a `{done}/{n}` header, in the orchestrator's pick order (not renderer-recomputed).
- **Done when:** a completed issue's row shows its PR URL sourced from the done-transition handoff
  read.
- **Done when:** a running row shows its active `exec:*` step and a queued row shows the issues it
  waits on.
- **Done when:** a non-TTY render of the multi-row queue emits zero ANSI and zero stdout bytes
  (NFR-4) and the disable switch reverts to the flat stream.

## Assumptions

- `plan.order` entries carry `title` and `blockers` at queue-build time, so title and deps need no new
  fetch. *(verified)*
- The done-transition already reads the handoff (`pr_urls`), so threading it into the item is a
  wiring change, not a new read. *(verified)*
- `QueueItem` is `frozen` and replaced (not mutated) in `_mark_queue`, so new fields with defaults
  keep existing call sites valid. *(verified)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** the renderer re-sorts or re-derives queue order and diverges from the orchestrator's pick
  order, so the queue lies. *Mitigation:* the row data comes from the orchestrator-built queue;
  position is the source of truth, asserted by an order-preservation test.
- **Risk:** the PR URL is read too early (before finish) and renders empty or stale on a done row.
  *Falsifier:* a done row with an empty PR field means the URL was not threaded from the
  done-transition handoff read — wire it at the `done` mark, not at build.

- [ ] Thread `pr_urls` into the item at the done-transition and render `done · <pr-url>` on completed rows. Done when: a completed issue's row shows its PR URL sourced from the done-transition handoff read, not recomputed. Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·L·M·L

# N09 — Footer line: turn · tokens · peak · elapsed

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** the run metrics on their own footer line with peak
> tokens, **so that** the stepper row stays about steps and I can read turn, token, peak, and elapsed
> at a glance.

> **▶ On pickup — before coding:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build agent's
> at-pickup task breakdown phase.
> **Blocked by:** N07 — the footer is a dedicated line in the owned region.

The proof-of-life metrics are folded into the stepper row today. This node gives them the prototype's
dedicated footer and adds peak-context tokens, which the orchestrator already computes.

## What

Move the `turn · tokens · elapsed` sub-status out of the stepper row into a dedicated footer line in
the owned region, and add peak-context tokens — the orchestrator's `on_progress` shim already carries
`peak_context_tokens`; the renderer's `on_progress` signature gains the peak argument to render it.
The footer reads `turn N · X tok (peak Y) · Z.Zs`.

## Why

The assumption being tested: peak tokens is already computed and threaded to the orchestrator's
progress shim, so surfacing it is a signature change, not a new measurement. The rejected alternative
is leaving metrics in the stepper row: it mixes step state with run metrics on one line and has no
room for peak. A dedicated footer separates the two concerns and reads like the prototype.

## Completion

- **Done when:** the footer renders `turn N · X tok (peak Y) · Z.Zs` and the stepper row no longer
  carries metrics.
- **Done when:** a non-TTY render emits zero footer bytes (NFR-4) and the `_UsageAccumulator` token
  totals are identical with the footer on and off (NFR-2).

## Assumptions

- The orchestrator's `on_progress` shim already passes `peak_context_tokens`, so the renderer only
  needs to accept and render it. *(verified)*
- The owned region (N07) can hold a third line for the footer below the queue and stepper.
  *(to-verify)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** widening the renderer's `on_progress` signature breaks the worker's progress callback
  contract. *Mitigation:* the orchestrator shim already computes peak; the change threads an existing
  value, covered by the progress-callback test.
- **Risk:** the footer line reads or counts tokens differently and perturbs the accounting path.
  *Falsifier:* a token-total mismatch with the footer on versus off (NFR-2) means the footer touched
  the accounting path — it must read the snapshot, not the accumulator.

## Tasks

- [ ] Move `turn · tokens · elapsed` into a dedicated footer line in the owned region and add peak-context tokens by widening the renderer's `on_progress` to accept the peak the orchestrator already passes. Done when: the footer renders `turn N · X tok (peak Y) · Z.Zs` and the stepper row no longer carries metrics. Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·L·L·L
- [ ] Guard non-TTY parity and token-accounting neutrality for the footer. Done when: a non-TTY render emits zero footer bytes (NFR-4) and `_UsageAccumulator` totals are identical with the footer on and off (NFR-2). Model: Fast · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = L·L·L·M·L

# N11 — Vertical persona drill-down

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** the active review step to show the full persona fan-out
> — each persona on its own row with its state and verdict — **so that** during review I can see which
> personas have cleared, which is running, and which still wait, on any worker.

> `exec:review`.

This is the deepest gap and the only cross-repo node. The strip shows at most one inline persona
today; the fan-out cannot be derived from existing artifacts — drain-cycle does not know the persona
roster (it lives in the pack), and no per-persona state or verdict exists. N10 settles the contract;
this node writes and renders it. Its first task exercises the real cross-repo write, so the
integration risk is retired on day one.

## What

Have `exec:review` write the persona roster (all `queued`) on entry and per-persona verdicts under
separate keys, per N10's shape; have the renderer read the roster and draw the vertical fan-out under
the active step — each persona with `✓ / ▶ / · / ✗` marks (state from the roster plus
`_active.persona`, verdict from the per-persona keys). Prove it on both a Claude worker and a codex
fixture (NFR-6). Degrade cleanly: an old pack with no roster falls back to N03's single inline
persona.

## Why

The assumption being tested: per-persona state belongs on a pack-authored marker, not the stream —
inline personas emit no tool boundary, so only the marker carries the fan-out on every worker. The
rejected alternative is deriving personas from the stream `Agent` blocks (design-doc Alt 2): the
captured stream shows `Agent` input has no structured persona field, so it dies on non-Claude workers
and couples the view to Claude internals. This closes KR2's persona-fan-out clause, the
worker-agnostic case the marker contract exists to serve.

  queued/running/done derived from the roster and `_active.persona`, on a Claude worker.

  yields the correct fan-out (NFR-6).

  a malformed roster leaves the exit code unchanged (NFR-3).
- **Done when:** only the renderer module reads the roster and verdict keys — the import-guard passes.

# Delivery plan — live execution swimlanes

Shaped from an **accepted design doc**:
[`docs/design-docs/live-execution-swimlanes/design-doc.md`](../../design-docs/live-execution-swimlanes/design-doc.md)
(Accepted 2026-06-18; writing-editor + human crit review both clean). The design recommends
**Alt 3 (a non-gating active-marker contract) built on an Alt 2 stream-derived walking skeleton**,
delivered in two slices. This file-set carries that recommendation as a deliverable → node → task
hierarchy. The upstream shaping chain (idea → product spike → backend spike → design doc) lives
beside the design doc; this plan does not restate it.

## The outcome being delivered

The default drain-cycle run output is a flat append-only event stream that never names the active
`exec:*` step or review persona, so a multi-minute run reads as a black box exactly when the
operator wants to look away. The design doc's accepted outcome: at a glance the operator can tell
which step and persona is executing and what is done versus upcoming — for the issue in flight and
across the cycle queue — **without the supervisor gaining any decision-power over inside-phase
content** (the artifact boundary, architecture §5 / ADR 0002 / ADR 0030, must hold).

The work is two sequenced slices plus the decision that reconciles them with the boundary:

- A **non-gating active-marker** is the part the rest depends on: Layer 2 authors a display-only
  `_active` pointer the renderer shows but no decision path may read. This is a small architectural decision (a
  reusable "display-only reads across the boundary" pattern), so the plan's first node is an `adr`.
- **Slice 1** proves the stepper row cheaply, this-repo-only, from the stream `tool_use` drain-cycle
  already receives — no cross-repo work. It is the walking skeleton.
- **Slice 2** adds the cross-repo marker write (`agent-skills-shaper`) that delivers persona depth
  on every worker and decouples the view from Claude-Code stream internals.

## Traceability — D1 serves KR1

This deliverable lands under a **new** Linear project, **"Live execution swimlanes"** (team
Personal), mirroring the sibling watch-pane upgrade (ABA-386–390), which earned its own project
rather than folding into "Multi-agent collaboration for correctness". The accepted design doc
(ABA-409) is the project's design-doc record and is not re-created as a node here (the input *is*
the accepted design doc).

| KR | Claim | Served by |
|----|-------|-----------|
| **KR1** | During a live drain, the default (non-`-w`) output shows the correct active step within one transition of ground truth and the correct active persona during review — on **both** a Claude and a non-Claude (codex) worker — while a render-path fault changes the run's exit code by **0**. | **D1** |

**Ordering:** N01 (the non-gating-marker ADR) lands before N03, since the marker contract must obey
the display-only invariant and settle its carrier (OQ-3) before any skill writes it. N02 (slice 1)
is this-repo-only and depends on nothing — its pre-build gate (OQ-1, the stream `tool_use` shape) is
already cleared. N03 (slice 2) is blocked by both N01 (the decision) and N02 (the proven
step-derivation path it falls back to).

**Appetite:** ~3 issues. **Kill condition:** if slice 1 cannot redraw a status region over the
stderr append model without perturbing the worker stream or the clean-stdout contract, the
status-only layout is wrong for this surface — stop and re-open the design doc's render decision
(OQ-4) before paying the cross-repo cost of slice 2.

## Tree

```
live-execution-swimlanes/
├── README.md                                          ← initiative root (this file)
└── D1-live-execution-swimlanes/                        → milestone (new) · serves KR1
    ├── _deliverable.md
    ├── N01 … non-gating active-marker invariant         · adr            ← one-way door, plan-review · blocks N03
    ├── N02 … stream-derived walking skeleton            · story · skeleton
    └── N03 … marker contract — persona depth + agnostic · story          ← cross-repo (agent-skills-shaper)
```

## Hand-count manifest

| Tracker artefact | Source layer | Count |
|------------------|--------------|------:|
| Milestones | deliverables (`D*`) | **1** |
| Issues | nodes (`N*`) | **3** |
| Sub-issues | tasks (`- [ ]` lines) | **12** |

input.new_string:
- **Slice 2** adds the cross-repo marker write (`agent-skills-shaper`) that delivers persona depth
  on every worker and decouples the view from Claude-Code stream internals.

## The outcome being delivered — D2

D1 shipped a deliberately minimal status strip: it proves the active step and a glyph-only queue, so
it meets KR1's active-step-and-persona-correct claim. The design doc's "The render: status-only
swimlanes" section specified more than KR1 measured — done-versus-upcoming across the *whole* step
chain, a multi-row queue that names each issue and its status, the review-persona fan-out, and a
footer. D2 closes that gap and brings the default view to the design doc's full layout. KR1 is
already observed, so D2 carries its own outcome, KR2.

The work is six render features plus the one architectural decision the deepest feature reverses:

- N04–N06 ride the proven slice-1 strip with no owned region — the full stepper chain, a verdict
  flash, and richer keyboard controls.
- **N07** is the part the richer panes depend on: an owned multi-line region (a fixed DECSTBM scroll
  region) that holds a status block the scrolling worker log cannot corrupt. It re-settles the design
  doc's render decision (OQ-4) for the taller view.
- N08 (richer queue rows) and N09 (footer) render into that region.
- **N10** amends ADR 0032 — its single-string persona rule forbids the fan-out — so the cross-repo
  persona work (N11) writes against a settled per-persona, display-only shape.

## Traceability — D1 serves KR1, D2 serves KR2

# Delivery plan — live execution swimlanes

Shaped from an **accepted design doc**:
[`docs/design-docs/live-execution-swimlanes/design-doc.md`](../../design-docs/live-execution-swimlanes/design-doc.md)
(Accepted 2026-06-18; writing-editor + human crit review both clean). The design recommends
**Alt 3 (a non-gating active-marker contract) built on an Alt 2 stream-derived walking skeleton**,
delivered in two slices. This file-set carries that recommendation as a deliverable → node → task
hierarchy. The upstream shaping chain (idea → product spike → backend spike → design doc) lives
beside the design doc; this plan does not restate it.

## The outcome being delivered

The default drain-cycle run output is a flat append-only event stream that never names the active
`exec:*` step or review persona, so a multi-minute run reads as a black box exactly when the
operator wants to look away. The design doc's accepted outcome: at a glance the operator can tell
which step and persona is executing and what is done versus upcoming — for the issue in flight and
across the cycle queue — **without the supervisor gaining any decision-power over inside-phase
content** (the artifact boundary, architecture §5 / ADR 0002 / ADR 0030, must hold).

The work is two sequenced slices plus the decision that reconciles them with the boundary:

- A **non-gating active-marker** is the part the rest depends on: Layer 2 authors a display-only
  `_active` pointer the renderer shows but no decision path may read. This is a small architectural decision (a
  reusable "display-only reads across the boundary" pattern), so the plan's first node is an `adr`.
- **Slice 1** proves the stepper row cheaply, this-repo-only, from the stream `tool_use` drain-cycle
  already receives — no cross-repo work. It is the walking skeleton.
- **Slice 2** adds the cross-repo marker write (`agent-skills-shaper`) that delivers persona depth
  on every worker and decouples the view from Claude-Code stream internals.

## The outcome being delivered — D2

D1 shipped a deliberately minimal status strip: it proves the active step and a glyph-only queue, so
it meets KR1's active-step-and-persona-correct claim. The design doc's "The render: status-only
swimlanes" section specified more than KR1 measured — done-versus-upcoming across the *whole* step
chain, a multi-row queue that names each issue and its status, the review-persona fan-out, and a
footer. D2 closes that gap and brings the default view to the design doc's full layout. KR1 is
already observed, so D2 carries its own outcome, KR2.

The work is six render features plus the one architectural decision the deepest feature reverses:

- N04–N06 ride the proven slice-1 strip with no owned region — the full stepper chain, a verdict
  flash, and richer keyboard controls.
- **N07** is the part the richer panes depend on: an owned multi-line region (a fixed DECSTBM scroll
  region) that holds a status block the scrolling worker log cannot corrupt. It re-settles the design
  doc's render decision (OQ-4) for the taller view.
- N08 (richer queue rows) and N09 (footer) render into that region.
- **N10** amends ADR 0032 — its single-string persona rule forbids the fan-out — so the cross-repo
  persona work (N11) writes against a settled per-persona, display-only shape.

## Traceability — D1 serves KR1, D2 serves KR2

This deliverable lands under a **new** Linear project, **"Live execution swimlanes"** (team
Personal), mirroring the sibling watch-pane upgrade (ABA-386–390), which earned its own project
rather than folding into "Multi-agent collaboration for correctness". The accepted design doc
(ABA-409) is the project's design-doc record and is not re-created as a node here (the input *is*
the accepted design doc).

Both deliverables land under the same **"Live execution swimlanes"** Linear project (team Personal),
mirroring the sibling watch-pane upgrade (ABA-386–390), which earned its own project rather than
folding into "Multi-agent collaboration for correctness". The accepted design doc (ABA-409) is the
project's design-doc record and is not re-created as a node (the input *is* the accepted design doc).

|----|-------|-----------|
| **KR1** | During a live drain, the default (non-`-w`) output shows the correct active step within one transition of ground truth and the correct active persona during review — on **both** a Claude and a non-Claude (codex) worker — while a render-path fault changes the run's exit code by **0**. | **D1** |
| **KR2** | During a live drain, the default view renders the design doc's full status-only layout — the whole `exec:*` chain as done/active/upcoming, a multi-row cycle queue with per-issue status, the active step's review-persona fan-out, and a footer — each correct within one transition of truth, while the fitness contracts (NFR-2 token-parity, NFR-3 non-gating, NFR-4 off-TTY clean, byte-identical passthrough, the import-guard) stay green. | **D2** |

**Ordering — D1:** N01 (the non-gating-marker ADR) lands before N03, since the marker contract must
obey the display-only invariant and settle its carrier (OQ-3) before any skill writes it. N02
(slice 1) is this-repo-only and depends on nothing — its pre-build gate (OQ-1, the stream `tool_use`
shape) is already cleared. N03 (slice 2) is blocked by both N01 (the decision) and N02 (the proven
step-derivation path it falls back to).

**Ordering — D2:** N04–N06 ride the proven slice-1 strip and depend on nothing. N07 (owned region)
blocks N08, N09, and N11. N10 (the ADR-0032 amendment) blocks N11, which is also cross-repo
(`agent-skills-shaper`). Recommended execution order: N04 → N05 → N06 → N07 → N08 → N09 → N10 → N11.

**Appetite:** D1 ~3 issues (shipped); D2 ~8 issues. **Kill condition (D2):** if N07 cannot hold a
multi-line status region over the stderr append model without corrupting the worker passthrough or
the clean-stdout contract, the owned-region approach is wrong for this surface — stop before paying
N08/N09/N11, and reconsider whether the richer panes belong in the `-w` pane instead.

# N04 — Full stepper chain: done / active / upcoming

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** the stepper to show the whole `exec:*` chain at once —
> done, active, and upcoming — **so that** I can see where the run is in the *whole* journey, not just
> the steps it has already walked.

> **▶ On pickup — before coding:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build agent's
> at-pickup task breakdown phase.

This rides the proven slice-1 strip — still one line, no owned region, no cross-repo work. Today the
strip shows only *visited* steps plus the active one (prior steps collapse to `·`, upcoming steps are
invisible); this node renders the full canonical chain so the operator sees what is done versus
upcoming, the design doc's stated behaviour that N02 deferred.

## What

Render against a canonical ordered chain instead of `tracker.history`. Define the chain once —
`pickup → breakdown → build → review → verify → simplify → finish`, with `debug` shown inline only
when entered (an escalation, not a fixed slot) — and mark each step done `●` / active `◉` /
upcoming `○` from the active step (`_effective_active`) and the visited set. The two signal sources
disagree on names — the stream gives `exec:pickup`, the `_active` marker gives bare `review` — so a
single normalization helper strips the `exec:` prefix and maps both onto the same chain slot, by
construction rather than by two parallel rules.

## Why

The assumption being tested: the operator's trust comes from seeing the *whole* path, and the chain
is fixed and known, so the renderer can draw upcoming steps without any new signal — a pure local
change on the already-proven strip. The rejected alternative is leaving the chain stream-derived
(visited-only): it cannot show what has not happened yet, which is half of "done versus upcoming."
This is the cheapest, lowest-risk gap to close and ships value before the owned region (N07) is
built.

## Completion

- **Done when:** a synthetic step sequence renders every canonical step with the correct
  done/active/upcoming mark within one transition of ground truth (NFR-1), `debug` appearing inline
  only once entered.
- **Done when:** a stream `exec:pickup` and a bare-`pickup` `_active` marker resolve to the same
  chain slot through the one normalization helper.
- **Done when:** a non-TTY render of the full chain emits zero ANSI control sequences and zero stdout
  bytes (NFR-4), and the disable switch still reverts to today's flat stream.

## Assumptions

- The canonical chain is fixed and complete (`pickup → … → finish`, `debug`/`simplify` as
  escalations) and matches the pack's `exec:*` workflow. *(to-verify)*

# N05 — Verdict flash on GO / NO-GO

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** a one-line flash when review or verify resolves —
> `verdict: NO-GO — looping back to build` — **so that** I can tell a gate passed or failed without
> reading the scrolling log.

> **▶ On pickup — before coding:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build agent's
> at-pickup task breakdown phase.

This is append-safe: the flash is a normal newline-terminated line emitted above the redrawn strip,
not part of any redraw region, so the node needs no owned region (N07) and ships on the slice-1
strip. It reads the same aggregate verdict the supervisor already consumes, for display only.

## What

On a verdict transition, read `review.verdict` and `verify.verdict` from `exec-state.json` through
the existing handoff reader (`_review_to_verdict`) and emit a one-line flash — GO in green, NO-GO in
red. The read is display-only and lives in the renderer module so the import-guard holds. Note the
live pack does not yet write a JSON `review` section, so on current packs the flash fires on
`verify.verdict`; the review-verdict flash lights up once the pack writes that section (the contract
N10/N11 establish).

## Why

The assumption being tested: the verdict the operator most wants — pass or fail — is already in an
artifact the supervisor reads, so surfacing it is a display-only read, not a new signal or a new
gate. The rejected alternative is parsing the worker's free text for "GO"/"NO-GO": brittle, and it
re-derives a value the artifact already states. The flash stays append-only so it carries no
owned-region risk and can land before N07.

## Completion

- **Done when:** a fixture with `verify.verdict` GO or NO-GO emits the right flash text and colour
  once on the transition, and an absent verdict emits nothing.
- **Done when:** the new verdict read lives only in the renderer module — the import-guard test still
  passes (no decision path reads it).
- **Done when:** a malformed verdict leaves `WorkerResult` and the exit code unchanged (NFR-3), and a
  non-TTY run emits zero flash bytes (NFR-4).

## Assumptions

# N06 — Richer keyboard controls: navigate and follow-toggle

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** to walk the queue with `↑/↓` and toggle auto-follow
> with `f`, **so that** I can hold my view on one issue's swimlane without losing my place when the
> running issue changes.

> **▶ On pickup — before coding:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build agent's
> at-pickup task breakdown phase.

The strip already maps digit keys `1`–`9` to focus and `0` to clear, on top of the focus machinery
(`focus_issue`, `_resolve_focus`). This node adds relative navigation and a follow toggle. Pause is
deliberately out of scope — a live `claude` cannot be paused; the ticket records why.

## What

Extend `KeyboardListener.handle_key` on the existing focus machinery: `↑/↓` (or `j/k`) move focus to
the previous or next queue item; `f` toggles auto-follow — on, the view follows the running issue
(today's default); off, it holds the manual selection; `q` signals the listener to stop, cosmetically,
never killing the run. Arrow keys arrive as escape sequences (`\x1b[A`), so the cbreak read loop
needs minimal multi-byte handling.

## Why

The assumption being tested: relative navigation and a follow toggle are the controls the operator
reaches for once the queue has more than a handful of issues, and they sit directly on the focus
machinery slice 1 already built — no new state. The rejected alternative is leaving only absolute
digit-focus: it does not scale past nine issues and offers no way to hold a view against auto-follow.
This stays on the current single-line queue, so it carries no owned-region dependency.

## Completion

- **Done when:** `handle_key` for `↑`/`↓` moves focus to the previous/next queue item and `f` toggles
  between follow-the-running-issue and hold-the-selection, driven through the `handle_key` test seam.
- **Done when:** `q` signals the listener to stop with `WorkerResult` and the exit code unchanged
  (NFR-3 — the control is cosmetic, never a kill).
- **Done when:** a non-TTY stdin constructs no thread and no termios state — byte-for-byte equivalent
  to never constructing the listener.

## Assumptions

- `focus_issue` / `_resolve_focus` already express both the auto-follow default and an explicit hold,
  so the toggle needs only a flag, not new focus state. *(verified)*
- Arrow-key escape sequences can be read in the existing cbreak loop with minimal multi-byte
  buffering. *(to-verify)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** multi-byte escape parsing misreads an arrow as separate `\x1b` / `[` / `A` keystrokes and
  mis-routes focus. *Mitigation:* the cbreak loop buffers the escape sequence; the `handle_key` seam
  is tested with the full sequence and with a bare `\x1b`.
- **Risk:** a new control path reaches into the run and stops it, breaking the non-gating ceiling.
  *Falsifier:* a `q` keystroke that changes the exit code means the listener is wired to execution —
  it must only set its own stop event.

## Tasks

Done when: `handle_key` for `↑`/`↓` moves focus to the adjacent queue item and `f` toggles follow vs hold, via the `handle_key` seam. # N07 — Owned multi-line status region (DECSTBM)

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** the status view to hold a stable multi-line region that
> the scrolling worker log cannot corrupt, **so that** the queue, stepper, and persona fan-out can
> share the screen with the live log without smearing into each other.

> **▶ On pickup — before N08, N09, N11:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build
> agent's at-pickup task breakdown phase. This is the **foundational** node for D2's richer panes.
> **Blocks:** N08, N09, N11 — each renders into the region this node establishes.

This settles the design doc's render decision (OQ-4) a second time, for the richer view. Slice 1
answered OQ-4 with a one-to-two-line strip redrawn by cursor-up, which assumes the cursor sits where
the renderer left it — a worker log line landing mid-redraw corrupts a taller block. This node owns a
region the log cannot reach, and it carries the integration risk for every richer pane, so its first
task exercises the real seam against a live stream.

## What

Pin the bottom N lines as a fixed status region with a DEC scroll region (DECSTBM, `\x1b[<top>;<bottom>r`)
and paint the status block with absolute cursor positioning while the worker passthrough scrolls in
the region above. The decision recorded in-node: a DECSTBM scroll region, not `rich.Live` or an
alternate screen — it is the only mechanism that keeps the append-only passthrough visible (the
property slice 1 protects), cohabits with the log (they never share cursor space), and stays inside
the fitness contracts. Its new cost is real and in scope: the region must reset on every exit path
(clean teardown and crash/kill), and re-pin on terminal resize.

## Why

The assumption being tested: a fixed bottom region driven by DECSTBM lets a multi-line status block
coexist with the scrolling worker log without the regression `rich.Live` would force (owning the
cursor, suppressing the passthrough). The rejected alternative is the alternate-screen buffer with
the passthrough suppressed: it reaches full prototype fidelity but drops the live `│` diagnostics the
operator relies on — a visibility regression the design deliberately avoided. Proving the region here
retires the render risk before N08/N09/N11 pay to fill it.

## Completion

- **Done when:** during a live drain the status block holds in a fixed bottom region while the
  `AgentSink` passthrough scrolls above it without corrupting the block, on a real TTY.
- **Done when:** the scroll region is released (`\x1b[r`) on normal teardown, on Ctrl-C, and on a
  killed worker — asserted by a teardown test — leaving the terminal with no residual region.
- **Done when:** a `SIGWINCH` during a live render re-pins the region to the new terminal size with
  the status block intact.
- **Done when:** the non-TTY render emits zero bytes (NFR-4), the passthrough sink bytes are
  byte-identical to a feature-off run, and an injected render fault leaves the exit code unchanged
  (NFR-3) — all for the multi-line region.

## Assumptions

- A DECSTBM scroll region keeps the worker passthrough confined to the scrolling area without
  changing the bytes `AgentSink` writes. *(to-verify)*
- The kill path can reach a region-reset before the terminal is handed back (an `atexit` or signal
  handler fires on the process-group kill). *(to-verify)*
- `shutil.get_terminal_size()` plus a `SIGWINCH` handler is enough to re-pin on resize without a full
  terminal-capability library. *(to-verify)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** a crash or kill skips the region reset and leaves the operator's shell wedged in a pinned
  region. *Mitigation:* the reset is registered on both the clean teardown seam and an
  `atexit`/signal handler; the teardown test asserts a reset on the kill path. This is the node's main
  risk.
- **Risk:** the passthrough and the renderer race on the same stderr and the absolute-positioned write
  lands inside the scrolling region. *Falsifier:* if the block corrupts under concurrent passthrough,
  the region is not actually confining the log — re-confirm the DECSTBM top/bottom bounds before
  building N08.
- **Risk:** a terminal that ignores DECSTBM (or a non-VT pipe) renders the block wrong. *Mitigation:*
  every escape stays behind the TTY check (NFR-4), so a non-TTY degrades to the flat stream with zero
  control bytes.

## Tasks

- [ ] `skeleton` — pin a fixed bottom region with DECSTBM against a real drain stream and paint the existing queue+stepper into it while the passthrough scrolls above, toolchain (terminal-size read) folded in. # N08 — Richer queue rows: title, status, counter

> **As** the drain-cycle operator, **I want** each queue row to name its issue and its status — title,
> running step, PR link, or what it waits on — with a done/total counter, **so that** I can read the
> whole cycle's state at a glance instead of decoding a row of glyphs.

> **▶ On pickup — before coding:** break this node into task-sized pieces using your build agent's
> at-pickup task breakdown phase.
> **Blocked by:** N07 — the multi-row queue renders into the owned region N07 establishes.

The queue is one line of glyphs and IDs today. This node makes it the prototype's multi-row pane:
glyph + ID + title + per-state status text and a `{done}/{n}` header. Most of the data is already in
hand at queue-build time; only the PR URL arrives later in the lifecycle.

## What

Grow `QueueItem` (today `identifier` + `state`) with `title` and `blocked_by`, populated at
queue-build from `plan.order`'s `title` and `blockers` — a pure local change, no new fetch. Thread
`pr_urls` into the item at the done-transition (`_mark_queue`) from the handoff data already read.
Render each row with its title and per-state status (`running · <active step>`, `queued · after
<deps>`, `done · <pr-url>`) and a `{done}/{n}` header, in pick order — never re-sorted — inside the
owned region. Add the new fields with defaults so existing construction sites and tests stay valid.

## Why

The assumption being tested: the queue's title, dependencies, and PR link are already available to
the orchestrator (`plan.order` and the handoff read), so the richer pane is plumbing existing data
into `QueueItem`, not a new data source. The rejected alternative is having the renderer re-derive
order or status from a different rule than the orchestrator picks — the queue would then lie about

# N09 — Footer line: turn · tokens · peak · elapsed

> tokens, **so that** the stepper row stays about steps and I can read turn, token, peak, and elapsed
> at a glance.

> **Blocked by:** N07 — the footer is a dedicated line in the owned region.

The proof-of-life metrics are folded into the stepper row today. This node gives them the prototype's
dedicated footer and adds peak-context tokens, which the orchestrator already computes.

## What

Move the `turn · tokens · elapsed` sub-status out of the stepper row into a dedicated footer line in
the owned region, and add peak-context tokens — the orchestrator's `on_progress` shim already carries
`peak_context_tokens`; the renderer's `on_progress` signature gains the peak argument to render it.
The footer reads `turn N · X tok (peak Y) · Z.Zs`.

## Why

The assumption being tested: peak tokens is already computed and threaded to the orchestrator's
progress shim, so surfacing it is a signature change, not a new measurement. The rejected alternative
is leaving metrics in the stepper row: it mixes step state with run metrics on one line and has no
room for peak. A dedicated footer separates the two concerns and reads like the prototype.

## Completion

- **Done when:** the footer renders `turn N · X tok (peak Y) · Z.Zs` and the stepper row no longer
  carries metrics.
- **Done when:** a non-TTY render emits zero footer bytes (NFR-4) and the `_UsageAccumulator` token
  totals are identical with the footer on and off (NFR-2).

## Assumptions

- The orchestrator's `on_progress` shim already passes `peak_context_tokens`, so the renderer only
  needs to accept and render it. *(verified)*
- The owned region (N07) can hold a third line for the footer below the queue and stepper.

  value, covered by the progress-callback test.
- **Risk:** the footer line reads or counts tokens differently and perturbs the accounting path.
  *Falsifier:* a token-total mismatch with the footer on versus off (NFR-2) means the footer touched
  the accounting path — it must read the snapshot, not the accumulator.

## Tasks

# N10 — Amend ADR 0032: per-persona display-only marker state

**Type:** `adr`. ADR 0032 settled `_active.persona` as a single string, last-write-wins, and
explicitly rejected richer persona state to avoid read-modify-write races. The persona fan-out (N11)
needs per-persona state, which reverses that decision — a real architectural change, settled and
plan-reviewed before any skill writes the new shape.

> **▶ On pickup — before N11:** record the amendment through the ADR discipline. Run the plan-review
> gate: this reverses a prior accepted decision on the shared supervisor↔pack boundary (ADR 0030 /
> 0032).
> **Blocks:** N11 — the persona drill-down must write against the settled shape, and the display-only
> invariant must hold before any skill writes it.

## What

Amend ADR 0032 so the pack may author a display-only **per-persona roster and state** alongside the
existing single `_active.persona`, while keeping every read non-gating (no advancement, halt, grade,
retry, exit-code, or stop-guard path may read it). The amendment settles the **race-free write rule**:
`exec:review` writes the full roster once on entry (all `queued`); the existing last-write-wins
`_active.persona` marks the running one; the renderer derives `done` for any persona before it in the
roster order — no per-member read-modify-write. Optional per-persona verdicts ride under separate keys
(`review.persona_verdicts.<name>`) so concurrent writers never share a key.

## Why

The assumption being tested: per-persona state can be display-only and race-free at once — a
write-once roster plus single-key verdicts avoids the read-modify-write contention that made ADR 0032
choose a single string, without making the supervisor decide on any of it. The rejected alternative
is a mutable shared `personas[]` array each sub-agent edits in place: that is exactly the race ADR
0032 rejected. Accepting this unlocks N11; until it lands, the persona contract is unsettled and the
single-string rule still forbids the fan-out.

## Completion

**Decision:** the pack may write a display-only per-persona roster (write-once, all `queued`) and
per-persona verdicts under separate keys; the renderer derives queued/running/done from the roster
order and the single `_active.persona`; no decision path may read any of it. Recorded as an amendment
to ADR 0032 with context and consequences, citing ADR 0030 and architecture §5, and naming the
enforcement: the import-guard (only the renderer module reads the new keys) and an NFR-3
fault-injection test on a malformed roster. The amendment states backward-compatibility — `handoff`
reads ignore unknown keys — and that an old pack writing no roster degrades to the single inline
persona. The ADR template discipline is not re-authored here; it lives in the ADR skill.

## Assumptions

- `exec-state.json` reads ignore unknown keys, so an additive roster and per-persona verdict keys are
  backward-compatible with `handoff.read*`. *(verified)*
- A write-once roster plus single-key per-persona verdicts avoids read-modify-write contention under a
  Claude-Code parallel persona fan-out. *(to-verify)*
- The display-only invariant stays enforceable by the import-guard once the new keys exist (only the
  renderer module reads them). *(to-verify)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** the roster or verdict keys are written in a shape that still races under parallel
  sub-agents, reintroducing the hazard ADR 0032 avoided. *Falsifier:* if any write needs to
  read-modify-write a shared key, the shape is wrong — keep the roster write-once and verdicts on
  per-name keys.
- **Risk:** "display-only" is asserted but a later change reads a persona key in a decision path,
  breaking the boundary. *Mitigation:* the amendment mandates the import-guard; N11 lands it, and
  review treats any decision-path read of the persona keys as a boundary violation.

## Tasks

- [ ] Frame the amendment: a display-only per-persona roster and per-persona verdict keys extend `_active`, still non-gating, citing ADR 0030 / 0032 and architecture §5. Done when: the amendment states the new shape, the boundary citation, and that the display-only invariant and import-guard still hold. Model: Frontier · risk one-way · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·H·L·H·L · companions code-review-and-quality
- [ ] Settle the race-free write rule: roster written once (all `queued`), `_active.persona` marks running, renderer derives done from roster order; per-persona verdicts under separate keys. Done when: the ADR names the write rule that avoids per-member read-modify-write and the backward-compat argument (handoff ignores unknown keys). Model: Frontier · risk one-way · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·H·L
- [ ] Record enforcement and run the plan-review gate to acceptance. Done when: the ADR names the import-guard and the NFR-3 malformed-roster fault-injection as its fitness functions and a plan-review reference is filed with the decision accepted. 1	# Delivery plan — live execution swimlanes
2	
3	Shaped from an **accepted design doc**:
4	[`docs/design-docs/live-execution-swimlanes/design-doc.md`](../../design-docs/live-execution-swimlanes/design-doc.md)
5	(Accepted 2026-06-18; writing-editor + human crit review both clean). The design recommends
6	**Alt 3 (a non-gating active-marker contract) built on an Alt 2 stream-derived walking skeleton**,
7	delivered in two slices. This file-set carries that recommendation as a deliverable → node → task
8	hierarchy. The upstream shaping chain (idea → product spike → backend spike → design doc) lives
9	beside the design doc; this plan does not restate it.
10	
11	## The outcome being delivered
12	
13	The default drain-cycle run output is a flat append-only event stream that never names the active
14	`exec:*` step or review persona, so a multi-minute run reads as a black box exactly when the
15	operator wants to look away. The design doc's accepted outcome: at a glance the operator can tell
16	which step and persona is executing and what is done versus upcoming — for the issue in flight and
17	across the cycle queue — **without the supervisor gaining any decision-power over inside-phase
18	content** (the artifact boundary, architecture §5 / ADR 0002 / ADR 0030, must hold).
19	
20	The work is two sequenced slices plus the decision that reconciles them with the boundary:
21	
22	- A **non-gating active-marker** is the part the rest depends on: Layer 2 authors a display-only
23	  `_active` pointer the renderer shows but no decision path may read. This is a small architectural decision (a
24	  reusable "display-only reads across the boundary" pattern), so the plan's first node is an `adr`.
25	- **Slice 1** proves the stepper row cheaply, this-repo-only, from the stream `tool_use` drain-cycle
26	  already receives — no cross-repo work. It is the walking skeleton.
27	- **Slice 2** adds the cross-repo marker write (`agent-skills-shaper`) that delivers persona depth
28	  on every worker and decouples the view from Claude-Code stream internals.
29	
30	## The outcome being delivered — D2
31	
32	D1 shipped a deliberately minimal status strip: it proves the active step and a glyph-only queue, so
33	it meets KR1's active-step-and-persona-correct claim. The design doc's "The render: status-only
34	swimlanes" section specified more than KR1 measured — done-versus-upcoming across the *whole* step
35	chain, a multi-row queue that names each issue and its status, the review-persona fan-out, and a
36	footer. D2 closes that gap and brings the default view to the design doc's full layout. KR1 is
37	already observed, so D2 carries its own outcome, KR2.
38	
39	The work is six render features plus the one architectural decision the deepest feature reverses:
40	
41	- N04–N06 ride the proven slice-1 strip with no owned region — the full stepper chain, a verdict
42	  flash, and richer keyboard controls.
43	- **N07** is the part the richer panes depend on: an owned multi-line region (a fixed DECSTBM scroll
44	  region) that holds a status block the scrolling worker log cannot corrupt. It re-settles the design
45	  doc's render decision (OQ-4) for the taller view.
46	- N08 (richer queue rows) and N09 (footer) render into that region.
47	- **N10** amends ADR 0032 — its single-string persona rule forbids the fan-out — so the cross-repo
48	  persona work (N11) writes against a settled per-persona, display-only shape.
49	
50	## Traceability — D1 serves KR1, D2 serves KR2
51	
52	Both deliverables land under the same **"Live execution swimlanes"** Linear project (team Personal),
53	mirroring the sibling watch-pane upgrade (ABA-386–390), which earned its own project rather than
54	folding into "Multi-agent collaboration for correctness". The accepted design doc (ABA-409) is the
55	project's design-doc record and is not re-created as a node (the input *is* the accepted design doc).
56	
57	| KR | Claim | Served by |
58	|----|-------|-----------|
59	| **KR1** | During a live drain, the default (non-`-w`) output shows the correct active step within one transition of ground truth and the correct active persona during review — on **both** a Claude and a non-Claude (codex) worker — while a render-path fault changes the run's exit code by **0**. | **D1** |
60	| **KR2** | During a live drain, the default view renders the design doc's full status-only layout — the whole `exec:*` chain as done/active/upcoming, a multi-row cycle queue with per-issue status, the active step's review-persona fan-out, and a footer — each correct within one transition of truth, while the fitness contracts (NFR-2 token-parity, NFR-3 non-gating, NFR-4 off-TTY clean, byte-identical passthrough, the import-guard) stay green. | **D2** |
61	
62	**Ordering — D1:** N01 (the non-gating-marker ADR) lands before N03, since the marker contract must
63	obey the display-only invariant and settle its carrier (OQ-3) before any skill writes it. N02
64	(slice 1) is this-repo-only and depends on nothing — its pre-build gate (OQ-1, the stream `tool_use`
65	shape) is already cleared. N03 (slice 2) is blocked by both N01 (the decision) and N02 (the proven
66	step-derivation path it falls back to).
67	
68	**Ordering — D2:** N04–N06 ride the proven slice-1 strip and depend on nothing. N07 (owned region)
69	blocks N08, N09, and N11. N10 (the ADR-0032 amendment) blocks N11, which is also cross-repo
70	(`agent-skills-shaper`). Recommended execution order: N04 → N05 → N06 → N07 → N08 → N09 → N10 → N11.
71

73	multi-line status region over the stderr append model without corrupting the worker passthrough or
74	the clean-stdout contract, the owned-region approach is wrong for this surface — stop before paying
75	N08/N09/N11, and reconsider whether the richer panes belong in the `-w` pane instead.

15	# N10 — Amend ADR 0032: per-persona display-only marker state
16	
17	**Type:** `adr`. ADR 0032 settled `_active.persona` as a single string, last-write-wins, and
18	explicitly rejected richer persona state to avoid read-modify-write races. The persona fan-out (N11)
19	needs per-persona state, which reverses that decision — a real architectural change, settled and
20	plan-reviewed before any skill writes the new shape.
21	
22	> **▶ On pickup — before N11:** record the amendment through the ADR discipline. Run the plan-review
23	> gate: this reverses a prior accepted decision on the shared supervisor↔pack boundary (ADR 0030 /
24	> 0032).
25	> **Blocks:** N11 — the persona drill-down must write against the settled shape, and the display-only
26	> invariant must hold before any skill writes it.
27	
28	## What
29	
30	Amend ADR 0032 so the pack may author a display-only **per-persona roster and state** alongside the
31	existing single `_active.persona`, while keeping every read non-gating (no advancement, halt, grade,
32	retry, exit-code, or stop-guard path may read it). The amendment settles the **race-free write rule**:
33	`exec:review` writes the full roster once on entry (all `queued`); the existing last-write-wins
34	`_active.persona` marks the running one; the renderer derives `done` for any persona before it in the
35	roster order — no per-member read-modify-write. Optional per-persona verdicts ride under separate keys
36	(`review.persona_verdicts.<name>`) so concurrent writers never share a key.
37	
38	## Why
39	
40	The assumption being tested: per-persona state can be display-only and race-free at once — a
41	write-once roster plus single-key verdicts avoids the read-modify-write contention that made ADR 0032
42	choose a single string, without making the supervisor decide on any of it. The rejected alternative
43	is a mutable shared `personas[]` array each sub-agent edits in place: that is exactly the race ADR
44	0032 rejected. Accepting this is the prerequisite for N11; until it lands, the persona contract is
45	unsettled and the single-string rule still forbids the fan-out.
46	
47	## Completion
48	
49	**Decision:** the pack may write a display-only per-persona roster (write-once, all `queued`) and
50	per-persona verdicts under separate keys; the renderer derives queued/running/done from the roster
51	order and the single `_active.persona`; no decision path may read any of it. Recorded as an amendment
52	to ADR 0032 with context and consequences, citing ADR 0030 and architecture §5, and naming the
53	enforcement: the import-guard (only the renderer module reads the new keys) and an NFR-3
54	fault-injection test on a malformed roster. The amendment states backward-compatibility — `handoff`
55	reads ignore unknown keys — and that an old pack writing no roster degrades to the single inline
56	persona. The ADR template discipline is not re-authored here; it lives in the ADR skill.
57	
58	## Assumptions
59	
60	- `exec-state.json` reads ignore unknown keys, so an additive roster and per-persona verdict keys are backward-compatible with `handoff.read*`. *(verified)*
61	- A write-once roster plus single-key per-persona verdicts avoids read-modify-write contention under a Claude-Code parallel persona fan-out. *(to-verify)*
62	- The display-only invariant stays enforceable by the import-guard once the new keys exist (only the renderer module reads them). *(to-verify)*
63	
64	## Key Risks
65	
66	- **Risk:** the roster or verdict keys are written in a shape that still races under parallel
67	  sub-agents, reintroducing the hazard ADR 0032 avoided. *Falsifier:* if any write needs to
68	  read-modify-write a shared key, the shape is wrong — keep the roster write-once and verdicts on
69	  per-name keys.
70	- **Risk:** "display-only" is asserted but a later change reads a persona key in a decision path,
71	  breaking the boundary. *Mitigation:* the amendment mandates the import-guard; N11 lands it, and
72	  review treats any decision-path read of the persona keys as a boundary violation.

content.text:
Done. The seven gap-closing features are shaped into a verifiable delivery hierarchy through the `shape-delivery` skill, following your standards.

## What I produced

A new deliverable **D2 — Default view reaches the design doc's full swimlanes layout**, added to the existing `live-execution-swimlanes` plan (D1/N01–N03 already shipped as ABA-410–412). It serves a new outcome **KR2**, because KR1 (correct active step + persona) is already met — these features deliver the *rest* of the layout the design doc specified but slice 1 deferred.

**Eight nodes (N04–N11):**

| Node | Type | Feature |
|---|---|---|
| N04 | story | Full stepper chain — done/active/upcoming |
| N05 | story | Verdict flash on GO/NO-GO (append-safe) |
| N06 | story | Richer keyboard controls — navigate, follow-toggle |
| N07 | story | **Owned multi-line region (DECSTBM)** — foundational, blocks N08/N09/N11 |
| N08 | story | Richer queue rows — title, status, counter |
| N09 | story | Footer line |
| N10 | adr | **Amend ADR 0032** for per-persona display-only marker state — blocks N11 |
| N11 | story | Vertical persona drill-down (cross-repo) |

Each node carries the five required sections, tagged assumptions, mitigated/falsifiable risks, and a task list where every task has one `Done when:` clause and a `Model:` routing annotation. The two architectural decisions are placed the way D1 placed its equivalents: the rendering model is settled in-node (N07, like N02 settled OQ-4), and the ADR-0032 reversal gets its own `adr` node (N10).

**Both gates pass:** `walk-delivery-plan` → 2 milestones / 11 issues / 33 sub-issues (manifest MATCH); `check-plan-framing` → PASS on all 11 nodes. A writing-editor pass cleaned two prose items.

The plan file-set is at `docs/delivery-plans/live-execution-swimlanes/D2-prototype-fidelity-view/` (gitignored — Linear is the tracked representation).

**Next step:** these nodes aren't in Linear yet. Want me to create them as issues N04–N11 under the "Live execution swimlanes" project — with the `node:adr` label and non-build banner on N10, and the `blocks` relations (N07→N08/N09/N11, N10→N11) wired up?
